title: Building Geometry
objective: Place a point, then raise a vertical line from it.
learn: Points, vectors and lines — the atoms of every Grasshopper model.

nodes.need: a component that turns X and Y numbers into a point
nodes.hint: Vector › Point. It has X, Y and Z inputs.
nodes.correct: Construct Point combines X, Y and Z coordinates into a point. Z is unconnected, so it defaults to 0 and the point sits on the ground plane.

wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter stores points picked in Rhino — it doesn’t build one from numbers.
wrong.vector2pt: Vector 2Pt needs two existing points to make a direction. We don’t have any points yet.
wrong.unitX: Unit X makes a direction along X, not a location.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that turns X and Y numbers into a point.

nodes.hint: Vector › Vector. “Up” in Rhino is the Z axis.
nodes.correct: Unit Z outputs a vector of length 1 pointing up the world Z axis (times its factor F). Vectors are directions — they have no fixed position, so the preview draws them from the origin.

wrong.unitX: Unit X points sideways along the X axis — our line should rise vertically.
wrong.constructPoint: Construct Point makes a location, not a direction.
wrong.amplitude: Amplitude resizes an existing vector, but there is no vector to resize yet.
wrong.*: This slot needs a direction pointing straight up.

nodes.need: a line built from a start point, a direction and a length
nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. Look for S, D and L inputs.
nodes.correct: Line SDL draws a line from a Start point, in a Direction, for a Length. Ideal when you know where and which way, but not the end point.

wrong.line: Line needs two points (A and B). We have one point and a direction, so Line SDL fits better.
wrong.pipe: Pipe wraps a tube around an existing curve — there is no curve yet.
wrong.circle: Circle draws a round curve, not a straight one.
wrong.*: This slot needs a line built from a start point, a direction and a length.

check.prompt: Which input of Line SDL receives the Unit Z vector?
check.hint: S = start, D = direction, L = length. What does a vector describe?
check.correct: D is the direction. Without it Line SDL falls back to the X axis — watch the line swing upright now that it’s connected.

wrong.S: S expects the start point. A vector has a direction but no location.
wrong.L: L expects a number for the length — the Length slider is already wired there.
